verdict.outcome: THE KERNEL WORKS AND IS EXACT, BUT IT IS SLOWER. Not adopted.

equivalence.reading: 1.788e-07 is f32 round-off, so the kernel computes the same function as the six-roll reference, not an approximation of it

verdict.why_slower: The only tile mosaic_gpu would accept is DEGENERATE: one site in x and one in y. With a 1x1 tile the six neighbours cannot be reused from SRAM, so every site is fetched seven times from GMEM -- strictly worse traffic than six materialised rolls, which read each site once per roll. That is also why the gap WIDENS with B, from +5.1% to +42.6%.
verdict.the_tile_is_fixed: The sawtooth claim does hold structurally: this tile does not change with B, so that kernel's sawtooth is gone by construction. But it costs 5-43%, and the sawtooth it removes is at most 15%, so it is not worth it for that either.

eight_refusals.msg: Only copies transferring a number of bytes divisible by the warpgroup size are supported. Got bytes=18252
eight_refusals.cause: a whole layer-plane is N*N*3 = 4563 elements, odd for EVERY geometry since N = 2(floor(Rd)+1)+1 is always odd
keeping the plane forces a batch tile that is a multiple of 32, and 32 whole planes need 570 KB against an H100 SM's 228 KB

eight_refusals.msg: async_copy requires all GMEM strides except the last one to be a multiple of 16 bytes
eight_refusals.cause: THE REAL BLOCKER. The innermost axis holds 3 spin components and 3*4 = 12 B is not a multiple of 16, which poisons every enclosing stride: x 12 B, y 468 B, z 18252 B, batch 91260 B, all four fail
eight_refusals.fix: pad the component axis 3 -> 4; then 16, 624, 24336, 121680 B all pass, the fourth component stays zero so the physics is exact, and the batch tile requirement drops

eight_refusals.msg: must have a number of elements that is a multiple of 128 (got 1248)
eight_refusals.cause: the rule is 128 ELEMENTS, not 128 bytes; I had it wrong

eight_refusals.msg: Unimplemented primitive in Pallas Mosaic GPU lowering: concatenate

jnp.sum over the component axis for the normalisation
eight_refusals.fix: move the normalisation out of the kernel; it is a cheap elementwise pass and the stencil is the memory-bound part worth moving

conclusion: The Pallas route is blocked by the BACKEND'S MATURITY, not by our design. Every way of shifting data inside the kernel -- iota plus where, slicing a loaded array, slicing a ref, concatenate -- is unsupported in jax 0.10.2's mosaic_gpu lowering, and axis reductions are unsupported too. A non-degenerate tile REQUIRES in-kernel shifting, so the only tile that compiles is the one that destroys the memory-traffic advantage. The Layout list it does offer (WGMMA, TCGEN05, WGMMA_UPCAST) shows what it is built for: tensor-core matmul shapes, not general stencils.
what_would_change_this: A jaxlib where mosaic_gpu lowers concatenate, or array slicing, or axis reductions. Any ONE of the three would allow a real tile.
Writing the kernel in Triton directly through jax-triton or a custom call, which has none of these restrictions since XLA already emits Triton for this very fusion.
Accepting CUDA C++ with a custom call, which has no restrictions at all but leaves the JAX ecosystem.
